THE COMMUNITY LAB
Good ideas deserve a test drive.
Original JevFlow adaptations of patterns from community projects.
3 runnable recipes




01 / ROUTING
Pick the right model.
Give the router a task. See whether it calls for speed, reasoning, coding, or a general model.
task→code→review?
Inspired by BunsDev / TypeSafeAI ↗Selection only. No downstream model call.


02 / BROWSER AGENTS
Find the next click.
Describe a page and its available actions. Ask which step gets closer to the goal.
goal→open_docs
Inspired by browser-use / Jev Ultrafast ↗Snapshot evaluation. No browser is controlled.


03 / GAME LOGIC
Give a character a choice.
Change hunger, energy, and money. See how a character weighs eating, resting, working, or exploring.
hunger: 85→eat
Inspired by jammaru / Hundred ↗One decision. The full town lives in the original project.


Built here from scratch. Original creators are credited for the ideas. These recipes do not embed their applications or imply endorsement.


02 / A SMALL LAYER. A BIG DIFFERENCE.
Your workflow. Your threshold.
Your call.
01
Bring the context
Pass a ticket, a document, an agent action, or your current application state.
state: { ...yourContext }
02
Ask a focused question
Define what you need to know and the answer space your application expects.
choice · score · yes / no
03
Keep control of the action
Route the result, set a threshold, or hand uncertain cases to a human.
if (decision) { act(); }


03 / MADE FOR YOUR CODEBASE
Feels like software.
Because it is.
Explicit inputs. Typed outputs.
A decision boundary you can read.
One question.
A useful answer.
JevFlow keeps the recipe, model result, and action policy separate. Inspect the question, tune a threshold, then take the pattern into your own application.
